definition: In this historical source, girdle sensation means a feeling of tightness or pain encircling the body like a belt, mentioned as an early symptom in lathyrism. The passage does not give a fuller standalone description beyond this context.

provenance.scope: Source record dictionaryofpsyc02tuke:chars-42000-54000; pinned source text

reasons: The source only lists “a girdle sensation” among symptoms of lathyrism; it does not explicitly define the term as a belt-like feeling of tightness or pain encircling the body.
“Early symptom” is not stated in the passage for girdle sensation specifically, so that timing claim is an interpretation rather than directly supported wording.

The packet does not explicitly define “girdle sensation” as “tightness or pain encircling the body like a belt.” It only lists “a girdle sensation” alongside other symptoms (“pains in the lumbar region”), without further wording that matches “encircling…like a belt.”

The definition claims it is “mentioned as an early symptom.” The packet places “a girdle sensation” in the description of how the disease “breaks out suddenly” and then later “patients on awaking,” but it does not explicitly label “girdle sensation” as an early symptom within that timeline.
